claims.text: The target alloy is a multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy with chemically distinct lamellae, such as Al-rich and Cr-rich phases.
Accelerated coupled degradation at elevated temperature arises from differential oxidation kinetics between the distinct phases.
The Al-rich phase oxidizes more rapidly than the Cr-rich phase.
The rapidly oxidizing Al-rich phase forms a less-protective oxide.
Electrochemical contrast between Al-rich and Cr-rich regions can produce localized galvanic coupling, with Al-rich regions anodic and Cr-rich regions cathodic.
Galvanic coupling at chemically heterogeneous boundaries promotes localized corrosion and pit formation.
Elevated-temperature reciprocating wear can occur in the presence of a surface oxide layer.
Different oxide types form at phase boundaries because the constituent phases have different oxidation kinetics.
Sliding wear causes the inadequately protective oxide at heterogeneous phase boundaries to spall.
Oxide spallation exposes fresh reactive surfaces and thereby accelerates localized corrosion.
Repeated differential oxidation, galvanic corrosion, and wear-induced oxide removal create a self-perpetuating degradation cycle.
High oxygen partial pressure promotes differential oxidation, whereas low oxygen partial pressure favors more uniform oxidation.
The proposed controlled comparison changes oxygen partial pressure while holding temperature, sliding conditions, and wear load constant.
High oxygen partial pressure will produce a higher total degradation rate than the low-oxygen baseline.
High oxygen partial pressure will produce deeper corrosion pits through accelerated galvanic corrosion.
High oxygen partial pressure will increase wear damage through spallation of inadequately protective oxides.
More uniform oxidation under low oxygen partial pressure reduces galvanic effects and coupled degradation.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply at approximately 500–600 °C under the specified reciprocating-wear conditions.
Changing temperature or wear conditions outside the stated range may alter oxidation rates and wear behavior.
Exact degradation rates and quantitative acceleration thresholds remain uncertain without experimental calibration.
